text: dsh-plugin-wepre 是面向 DSH agent 会话的 WePre Next 发布工具。它向 DSH 注册验证码登录、登录状态查询、内容发布和质检报告查询工具，可将单屏 HTML 或 ZIP 卡片上传到 WePre Next，并返回发布版本和质检结果；质检失败时可查看各视口问题后更新同一内容。适合希望在 DSH 对话中制作并发布离线内容卡片的用户。需要 WePre Next 账号验证，或提供短期发布令牌；发布内容会发送至配置的 WePre Next 服务。

dsh-plugin-wepre adds tools to publish single-screen HTML or ZIP cards to WePre Next from DSH. It supports login, status lookup, publishing, and QA reports; failed checks return viewport issues for correction. A WePre account or token is needed, and card files are uploaded to the configured service.
想让 DSH 帮我把做好的单屏 HTML 卡片发布到 WePre。
发布内容被视口质检拦下后，怎么查看问题并继续修复更新？
我希望在 DSH 对话里完成登录，然后上传一个 ZIP 格式的离线内容卡片。
dsh-plugin-wepre 的功能「发布内容卡片」：wepre_publish 上传 index.html 或 ZIP，并可附标题、描述和版本信息。服务端返回内容标识、版本与质检状态；失败时提供视口问题以便修复更新。
dsh-plugin-wepre 的功能「登录与会话验证」：先请求短信或邮箱验证码，再登录并保存会话；状态查询工具可确认登录情况，供发布和报告查询使用。
dsh-plugin-wepre 发布卡片及查询质检信息时会请求配置的 WePre Next 服务，卡片文件随发布请求上传；默认服务域名为 wepre.cn。
dsh-plugin-wepre 发布需短期 token 或登录会话；token 可从 WEPRE_PUBLISH_TOKEN 读取，验证码登录所得会话写入本机 sessionFile。

dsh-plugin-wepre README · dsh-plugin-wepre：English | [中文](README.zh.md)

A [DeepSeek Harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness) (`dsh`) plugin that lets your agent publish single-screen content cards to [WePre Next](https://wepre.cn/next-test/) — a platform that pushes offline, single-viewport cards to users while they wait on AI generations.

With this plugin installed, a dsh session goes from "write me a card" to "it's live" in one conversation:

dsh-plugin-wepre README · dsh-plugin-wepre：```
you:   Build a pomodoro-timer card and publish it to WePre
agent: <writes index.html, calls wepre_publish>
agent: QA gate rejected it — OVERFLOW_Y at 390x600. Fixing… <edits, republishes>
agent: Published. contentId=cnt_xxx, version v1 (QA: passed)

dsh-plugin-wepre README · Install：```sh
dsh plugin --profile web add dsh-plugin-wepre
```

Verify the layer composed, then boot:

```sh
dsh --profile web --dump-config   # shows a "# == dsh-plugin-wepre" layer
dsh --profile web
```

No build step and no `prepare` script — installing from a git host works too:

```sh
dsh plugin --profile web add github:shujiTech/dsh-plugin-wepre
```

dsh-plugin-wepre README · What the agent gets：Five model-facing tools on `ctx.tools`:

| Tool | What it does |
|---|---|
| `wepre_request_code` | Send a one-time login code (SMS / email) |
| `wepre_login` | Redeem the code; the session cookie is persisted locally |
| `wepre_whoami` | Show current login state |
| `wepre_publish` | Upload an `index.html` / `.zip` card through the server-side QA gate |
| `wepre_qa_report` | Fetch the full QA report (per-viewport issues) for a content |

dsh-plugin-wepre README · What the agent gets：The tools' descriptions teach the model WePre's content rules (single-screen layout, no network calls, no external resources, the `wepre-next:execute` postMessage contract) and the QA fix loop: when the gate answers `QA_GATE_FAILED`, the agent reads the structured per-viewport issues, fixes the card, and republishes with the same `contentId` — no human in the loop.

dsh-plugin-wepre README · Authentication：`wepre_publish` / `wepre_qa_report` resolve credentials in this order:

1. **`token` config field** — a short-lived publish token from the WePre publish page
2. **`WEPRE_PUBLISH_TOKEN`** environment variable
3. **The stored login session** — created by `wepre_login`, persisted to `sessionFile` (default `~/.dsh/wepre-session.json`, mode `0600`)

dsh-plugin-wepre README · Authentication：For interactive use, just ask the agent to log in: *"log in to WePre with 13800138000"* — it will send the code, ask you for it, and store the session. For CI / headless (`dsh --profile headless "…"`), set a token.

dsh-plugin-wepre README · Configuration：Override the plugin row in your profile's `cordis.patch.yml` (a patch replaces the row's **whole** config — restate keys you keep):

```yaml
- id: wepre-publish
  name: dsh-plugin-wepre
  config:
    endpoint: 'https://wepre.cn/next-test'

| Key | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `endpoint` | `https://wepre.cn/next-test` | WePre Next site root |
| `token` | — | Short-lived publish token (Bearer) |
| `sessionFile` | `~/.dsh/wepre-session.json` | Persisted login session |

dsh-plugin-wepre README · What a publish call looks like：`wepre_publish` maps to `POST /next-test/api/next-contents` (multipart). Parameters: `title`, `path` (absolute, `.html` or `.zip`), `description`, `contentId` (for in-place version updates), `changeNote`, `versionLabel`, `downloadEnabled` (default `false`), and manifest fields `viewports` (`all`/`desktop`/`mobile`), `interaction` (`execute`/`passive`), `capabilities`.
section: What a publish call looks like

text: dsh-plugin-wepre README · What a publish call looks like：On success it returns `contentId`, `versionId`, `versionNumber` and the QA status. On `QA_GATE_FAILED` (HTTP 422) it returns the structured `issues` and `reportId` as a canonical value — not an exception — so the agent can iterate. Before uploading, the tool runs a local pre-flight scan for WePre's banned tokens (`fetch`, `localStorage`, `Worker`, `overflow:auto`, …) and external links, and reports them as non-blocking warnings.
section: What a publish call looks like

text: dsh-plugin-wepre README · Content rules in one paragraph：WePre Next cards are single-screen, offline, sandboxed pages: one `index.html` (or a zip with it at the root), root container at `100dvh` with `overflow:hidden`, no `overflow:auto/scroll`, no network calls / `localStorage` / `Worker` (the words are banned even in comments), no external or root-absolute URLs, and `execute`-mode cards must run their main action on the `wepre-next:execute` postMessage. The full contract: [WePre Next 内容发布规范](https://wepre.cn/next-test/) (see the publish guide on the site).

dsh-plugin-wepre README · Development：Plain ESM JavaScript, no build step. Behavioral tests drive the tools against a mock WePre server:

```sh
npm install
npm test
```
